nodes.description: The convergence point. The leptin to melanocortin to SIM1 axis is the pathway dysregulated across several monogenic obesity syndromes, and interrupting it at either the SIM1 or the POU3F2 step leaves appetite unrestrained. The clinical expression is hyperphagia and susceptibility to obesity rather than obesity as an inevitability - the deletion sets a predisposition that environment can amplify or blunt, which is why the phenotype is variable even within a family carrying the same deletion.

nodes.description: Developmental delay and intellectual disability are as consistent a part of the syndrome as the obesity and are not secondary to it. Both SIM1 and POU3F2 are neurodevelopmental transcription factors, and the delay is present in patients whose deletion is small enough to be POU3F2-only, so it is not simply a marker of how much chromosome has been lost.

nodes.description: The lesion is a heterozygous interstitial deletion of proximal 6q, usually de novo, whose extent varies between patients. That variability is the reason the syndrome resists a single-gene account: different deletions remove different combinations of dosage-sensitive genes, and the resulting phenotypes overlap without being identical. SIM1 at 6q16.3 is the gene most often invoked, and a separate ~350 kb critical region at 6q16.1 containing POU3F2 accounts for a smaller-deletion phenotype.

nodes.description: POU3F2 is a proneuronal transcription factor important for hypothalamic development, and zebrafish work places it downstream of SIM1 in the same pathway, controlling oxytocin expression in the neuroendocrine preoptic area. That ordering is what makes the two critical regions coherent rather than coincidental: deleting either gene interrupts the same axis at a different point, which is why the small POU3F2-only deletions reproduce the obesity and developmental phenotype without touching SIM1.

nodes.description: SIM1 is a transcription factor required for development of the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus, the structure through which melanocortin signalling acts on appetite. Halving its dose degrades that development. The strongest evidence that this step alone is sufficient comes from outside the deletion syndrome: sequencing SIM1 in obesity cohorts found rare variants whose loss-of-function severity in a transcriptional assay tracked the obesity risk they conferred within families - a rare instance where the functional grading and the family risk were measured on the same variants.
